# workflow

A deterministic progression engine for step graphs. Go 1.26+.
Module: github.com/deepnoodle-ai/workflow. Root depends only on stdlib and
github.com/deepnoodle-ai/expr.

The engine is one pure function:

    func Apply(def *Definition, st *State, ev Event) (*State, []Command, error)

It does no I/O, starts no goroutines, reads no clock except ev.At, and never
modifies st. The run's clock is max(ev.At, st.UpdatedAt): an event stamped
earlier than the last one applied is applied at that time. Hosts persist the returned State and Commands in one
transaction and carry out the commands after commit. Results come back as
events, at least once; duplicates are no-ops.

## Packages

- workflow (root): Load, LoadMap, Apply, Outstanding,
  State, Event, Command, StepID, StepError, RunError, Kinds, KindMap, Limits.
- local: Runner{Handlers, Save, Now}; Run(ctx, def, inputs, trigger) and
  Resume(ctx, def, st). Handler func(ctx, workflow.Command) (any, error).
  ctx done = pause (returns running state + ctx.Err(); Resume continues).
  Cancel the run: ctx, cancel := context.WithCancelCause(ctx);
  cancel(local.Cancel(reason)) -> runs finally steps (on a context the
  cancel does not reach), then returns the cancelled state, nil error.
- postgres (separate module, pgx v5): Store (New, Migrate, Start/StartTx,
  Deliver/DeliverTx, Cancel, GetRun, Steps, Events). Start, Deliver and
  Cancel return *Result{State, Commands, Applied}: Commands are already in
  the outbox (do not run them); Applied is false for a duplicate, late or
  finished-run event. WithOnFinished(fn) runs in the finishing tx (after
  finally steps; Finished carries FinallyErrors);
  RunsChannel() is notified on every status change. Worker{Store, Handlers,
  Concurrency, Lease, Poll, MaxClaims, ListenConfig}.Run(ctx), Handler
  func(ctx, Task) (any, error), ErrDeferred, ErrRunNotFound, ErrRunExists,
  ErrDefinitionUnavailable. Tasks are fenced by a token that only grows.
- cmd/workflow: `workflow validate FILE`, `workflow run FILE -input k=v -trigger FILE -json`.
  stdout is only the result (outputs JSON, or the state with -json); print
  steps, shell stderr and status go to stderr. Shell with: params become
  upper-cased env vars that override the inherited env. Ctrl-C cancels.

## Loading a definition

    def, err := workflow.Load(jsonBytes, workflow.KindMap{   // or workflow.LoadMap(yamlDecodedMap, kinds)
        "agent":  func(cfg map[string]any) error { ... },  // nil accepts anything
        "action": nil,
    })
    def.Limits = workflow.Limits{MaxOutputBytes: 256 << 10, MaxStateBytes: 8 << 20} // defaults

Load returns *ValidationError{Problems []Problem{Step, Message}} with
every problem, and no definition. Apply returns ErrNotValidated for a
Definition not made by Load.
def.Hash() is a sha256 of the canonical document; State.Definition stores it.

## Definition shape (JSON; YAML via LoadMap)

    {
      "name": "...", "description": "...",
      "inputs": {"repo": {"type": "string", "required": true, "default": ..., "description": "..."}},
      "steps": [ <step>, ... ],            // first step is the start step
      "on_failure": [ <step>, ... ],       // run once, in order, when the run fails; `error` is bound
      "finally": [ <step>, ... ],          // run once, in order, after the outcome is decided; `run` is bound
      "outputs": {"k": "${{ expr }}",          // optional; default: last step value of each ended path
                  "s": {"value": "${{ expr }}", "schema": <schema | name>, "description": "..."}},
      "schemas": {"name": <JSON schema>},  // named types
      "event_schema": <schema | name>      // types `event`; trigger validated at Start
    }

Step keys:
- name (identifier, unique across steps/on_failure/finally; not
  inputs/event/item/index/error/run or a function name)
- exactly one kind key: a host kind ("agent": "reviewer", "action": "x") or
  "join": [names] | "set": value | "sleep": "1h"
- with: {..} templates, evaluated at dispatch (host kinds only)
- each: expr producing a list; concurrency: n; continue_on_error: bool
- output: <schema | basic type | schema name>  (host kinds; validated on completion;
  sent as Command.OutputSchema)
- next: "name" | ["name", {"step": "name", "when": "bool expr"}]; match: "all" | "first"
  | {"switch": "expr", "cases": {"value": "step" | ["a","b"]}, "default": "step" | []}
- retry: {max_attempts, backoff: "1s", max_backoff: "5m", factor: 2, errors: [types]} | n
- catch: [{errors: [types], next: "name"}] | "name"
- timeout: "5m"; max_visits: n

Host-kind Config = the kind key plus every unreserved key (model,
instructions, ...), unevaluated. Reserved keys: name, description, output,
with, each, concurrency, continue_on_error, next, match, retry, catch,
timeout, max_visits, join, set, sleep.

Types: Load type-checks every expression (expr's Program.Check) against
input schemas, event_schema, step output schemas (or KindSchemas), inferred
set types, item/index, error. A step not settled on every path to the reader
is maybe-nil: read it with ?. or coalesce(a, b) (non-nil when a and b are
alternatives one of which must have run). outputs see a step as certain if
no completing run can skip it. On paths only a catch leads to, the step's
value is {error: {type, message}}. when must be boolean; a switch must
cover its enum or have a default (number keys are JSON: "1000000"). with:
(absent = {}) is checked against the kind's params schema; unions must fit
in every variant. Optional KindSchemas interface on Kinds:
Schemas(kind, config) (params, output *Schema, error). ParseSchema(json).
Load copies host schemas before resolving refs; it never modifies them.
Schema -> type: no type/enum ({}) = unchecked; type list = union of kinds
(null = nullable); enum = union of its values' kinds, filtered by type;
{type: object} with no properties = open object (fields unchecked);
properties = closed object, non-required = maybe-nil; additionalProperties
schema = open with that field type (read with ?.). Ref cycles (alias or
recursive) are rejected; inlined schemas are limited to 10000 nodes.
Outside the promise: untyped values (no schema, {}, event without
event_schema, inputs without an inputs block), list index out of range,
value errors (int("abc"), 1/0), number->integer and string->enum params
(checked at dispatch: invalid_params).
Runtime: inputs/trigger validated at Start, params at dispatch
(invalid_params), outputs at completion (invalid_output); absent declared
properties read as nil; every step name is in the env (nil until settled).
Outputs long form: an entry that is an object with a value or schema key
({value, schema, description}); the two forms mix. Load checks value's
type against schema like with: against params; at run completion each
value is validated: a mismatch fails the run (RunError type
invalid_output, no Step, on_failure runs). def.Outputs map[string]*Output
{Value any; Schema *Schema; Description string}; def.OutputSchema() *Schema
is the outputs as one JSON Schema object (all required, no others; nil
without outputs:), for exposing a workflow as a tool.

Expressions: each/when/switch are bare expr. with/set/outputs strings: no
${{ }} = literal; exactly one ${{ ... }} (no text or
spaces around it) = typed value; otherwise rendered text.
Only ${{ }} is a template: shell ${HOME} is text; $${{ writes a literal ${{.
Globals: inputs, event (trigger), steps by name, item/index in each with,
error in on_failure, run in finally: {status: "completed"|"failed"|"cancelled",
error: {step, step_id, type, message} or nil unless failed}. Extra functions: concat(lists...), coalesce(values...).
Keyword field names work: error.type.

Semantics:
- Multiple matching edges fork the path into children named
  "<path>.<target>". No match ends the path. Run completes when all paths end.
- join waits until no live path can reach it; merges arrivals into their
  common ancestor path; named steps must have settled on an arrival or the
  run fails (type "join"). join: [] names nothing.
- loops: a join fires once per pass of the loops it is in (a pass starts
  when a path enters the loop's head). It waits for paths that can still
  arrive in that pass, including paths going around loops it is not in.
  Named steps must have settled in the current pass of the loops they share
  with the join. Load rejects a join in a loop with several entry steps.
- each: one DispatchStep per item, parallel up to concurrency; output is the
  list of item outputs in order. An item failure (after retries) fails the step
  at once: items in flight get CancelStep, pending items are skipped, and
  late results for them are ignored. With continue_on_error, failed items
  become {error: {type, message}} instead.
- Retry only when declared AND StepError.Retryable AND type matches. New
  DispatchStep with Attempt+1 and NotBefore = At + backoff.
- timeout: ScheduleTimer with the attempt's StepID; on TimerFired the attempt
  gets CancelStep and fails with type "timeout" (retryable). Once the attempt
  settles the timer is obsolete; hosts may drop it, and a late TimerFired is
  a no-op.
- catch routes a terminal failure; the step's value becomes {error: {...}}.
- Run failure cancels everything in flight, then runs on_failure. An
  on_failure failure sets RunError.OnFailure and stops on_failure.
- Cancel: CancelStep for all in flight, no on_failure (a cancel during
  on_failure cancels it and the run is cancelled); then finally.
- finally: steps run in order once the outcome is decided (completed after
  outputs are evaluated; failed after on_failure; cancelled after in-flight
  work is cancelled). Same shapes as on_failure (host kinds and set; with,
  output, retry, timeout; no next/catch/each/join/sleep). They read run,
  every step/on_failure step as maybe-nil, and earlier finally steps (a
  failed one reads as {error: {type, message}}); not error, outputs or
  later finally steps. Each runs even if an earlier one failed. A failure
  never changes the outcome: it is appended to State.FinallyErrors and
  Command.FinallyErrors ([]*RunError) on the terminal command. Status while
  they run: completing | failing | cancelling; the terminal command comes
  after the last one. A cancel during finally cancels the step in flight,
  skips the rest (each reported, type "cancelled") and finishes with the
  outcome already decided (completed stays completed, with outputs).

## Events and commands

    type Event struct {
        At time.Time; Kind EventKind  // start | step_completed | step_failed | timer_fired | cancel
        Inputs, Trigger map[string]any // start
        StepID StepID; Output any; Error *StepError  // step events
        Reason string                  // cancel
    }
    type StepError struct { Type, Message string; Retryable bool }
    type Command struct {
        Kind CommandKind  // dispatch_step | cancel_step | schedule_timer | run_completed | run_failed | run_cancelled
        StepID StepID; Step, StepKind string
        Params, Config map[string]any; Item any; Index int (-1 without each); Attempt int
        NotBefore time.Time            // dispatch: retry backoff; timer: fire time
        Outputs map[string]any; Error *RunError; Reason string
        FinallyErrors []*RunError      // any terminal command
    }
    type RunError struct { Step string; StepID StepID; Type, Message string; OnFailure *RunError; At time.Time }

StepID format: <path>/<step>[@<visit>][[<index>]]#<attempt>, e.g.
main/verify[3]#1, main.tests/lint@2#1. Use it as the idempotency key.

Apply errors (host mistakes, state unchanged): ErrNotValidated,
ErrDefinitionMismatch, ErrNotStarted, ErrUnknownStep, ErrInvalidEvent,
ErrInvalidInputs. A duplicate or late event returns (st, nil, nil) with the
same pointer.

Limits: MaxOutputBytes caps one task output or set value; MaxStateBytes caps
State.Bytes, the outputs, set values and each items the state holds now. A
step visit a newer visit of the same step superseded (a loop pass) is dropped
from Nodes with its bytes, so a poll/sleep loop runs indefinitely; results for
a dropped visit are ignored as late. Nodes is not a history.

Library error types: timeout, expression, output_too_large,
state_too_large, join, max_visits, switch, invalid_output, invalid_params,
cancelled (finally steps a cancel stopped, in FinallyErrors).

## State

JSON-serializable. Fields: Definition (hash), Status (running | completing |
failing | cancelling | completed | failed | cancelled), Inputs, Trigger,
StartedAt, FinishedAt, UpdatedAt, Outputs, Error, Reason (cancel reason),
FinallyErrors, Paths, Nodes, Joins, Bytes. Helpers: st.InFlight()
[]StepID, st.Unit(id) *Unit (nil if superseded), RunStatus.Terminal()
(completed/failed/cancelled only), RunStatus.Outcome() (completing ->
completed, failing -> failed, cancelling -> cancelled).
Outstanding(def, st) rebuilds DispatchStep/ScheduleTimer commands for
in-flight work.

## Host contract

1. Persist state, step records and commands (outbox) in the event's transaction; lock the run row.
2. Carry out commands only after commit.
3. Deliver results at least once.
4. Make each attempt idempotent by StepID.
5. Store definitions by hash; a run keeps its version.
